units.spine: Nothing in Warmholz is arranged for buying and selling in quantity.
What gets done in Warmholz is never anybody's official post, only ever somebody's job on the side.
The stock and the people of Warmholz have been pulled inward, and the ground that was given up stands abandoned.
Nothing here is urgent, and the town's troubles are chronic rather than acute.
This is as far as Warmholz can go before it is no longer the same settlement, and that limit is close now.
It is getting worse, steadily rather than suddenly, and each season costs a little more than the one before.
The year in Warmholz ends close enough to level that it draws notice.
Only a part of what happens in Warmholz is ever known, and no one here decides which part.
Under the terms it currently has, Warmholz works, and the judgment falls on those terms, not the town.
Between Warmholz and trouble lies less room than a town this size ought to have.
What protects Warmholz is that nobody has wanted it, and the town understands the arrangement.
No answer exists in Warmholz for what lives beyond its fields, and the task of finding one falls to nobody.
More goes on in Warmholz than is kept track of, and little of it stays hidden.
Little is spare in Warmholz, and that is the first thing a careful eye notices.
Neither a practitioner nor any arrangement is kept in Warmholz, and no one expects either.
Nobody in Warmholz worries about food, and nothing here threatens the supply.
Where Warmholz stands is close enough to the road to matter, and no closer.
A handful of roofs with a reason behind them make up Warmholz, and the reason is usually the ground.
No marked relationship, friendly or hostile, ties Warmholz to anywhere else, and none is on record.
A careful reader of Warmholz finds one loose end, and it is the kind a single institution could tie off.
